title: SM90 (Hopper) support: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash end to end on 8x / 4x H20-3e
body:
## Summary

DeepInfer currently runs on SM100 and Ascend 950. This PR adds an SM90 (Hopper) path so that DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs end to end on Hopper GPUs, validated on 8x and 4x NVIDIA H20-3e (141 GB):

- same checkpoint, no conversion
- attention DP / CP, MoE EP, DSpark
- CUDA graphs on

Key design points:

- The MXFP4 routed experts stay resident in FP4, so 4 GPUs are enough.
- FlashMLA's last Hopper kernels (`ba89a34`) are extended to the V4.1 KV cache formats.

SM100 and Ascend behaviour is unchanged. Every SM90 path is selected by `PLATFORM.is_sm90`, and all new kernels live in `deepinfer/model_executor/layers/sm90_ops/`.

**Results on H20-3e** (details, settings and methodology below):

| | 8x H20-3e | 4x H20-3e |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TTFT, 128K input (context parallel) | 2.15 s | 3.64 s |
| TTFT, 512K input | 9.66 s | 16.72 s |
| TTFT, ~1M input | 22.2 s | 38.5 s |
| Decode, 64 concurrent, 1024 in / 512 out, total tok/s | 3793 | 2463 |
| GSM8K (1319, 8-shot) | 0.943 | 0.941 |

TTFT: one cold request at a time, median of 3, context parallel over all GPUs, NCCL all-gather overlapped with compute. Decode: random token ids, total output tok/s. The 8-GPU run uses the default prefill intervals; the only 4-GPU run used intervals 1 / 1. GSM8K: 8-shot completion, with the first 8 test questions as shots and all 1319 scored, as in SGLang's GSM8K harness.

A comparison with SGLang on the same hardware will follow in a comment.

## What changes on SM90

| Component | SM100 | SM90 (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sparse attention, prefill and decode (V41 MXFP8 SWA cache, V41_FP4 compressed cache) | FlashMLA `2e5429f` | `flash_mla_sm90`: FlashMLA `ba89a34` (its last Hopper kernels) plus a patch that adds the V4.1 KV formats |
| FP8 linears and the `wo_a` einsum (packed UE8M0 1x32 / 32x32 scales) | DeepGEMM | block-[32, 32] FP8 Gluon GEMM, tuned for every V4.1 linear shape |
| Sparse-indexer logits (FP4 index K; dense, candidate and paged rows) | DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4` MQA logits | Triton kernels plus a Gluon keys-major prefill kernel, following the reference indexer arithmetic |
| Routed experts (MXFP4) | Mega MoE / `fp8_fp4` grouped GEMM | non-mega EP path with humming W4A8 (FP4 resident; the default when installed), or `triton_fp8` / `hybrid` / `deepgemm` |
| MoE gate, mHC | `mega_gate`, `mega_mhc` | existing `moe_topk_gate` and TileKernels mHC |
| Top-k | DeepSelect `sm_100a` | DeepSelect also built for `sm_90a`, plus a vendor patch for the 16-CTA cluster kernel H20 cannot launch |
| CP all-gather | DeepEP `BucketBuffer` (needs NVLink multicast) | by default an NCCL all-gather buffer with the same interface; `BucketBuffer` with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1` where NVLink multicast works |
| Build | — | on SM90, `./build.sh` builds `flash_mla_sm90` and installs `humming-kernels`; `scripts/vendor_patches/` holds the DeepSelect, DeepEP and FlashMLA patches |

**Footprint.** 56 files, +9140 / −72 lines.

- 25 existing files: +567 / −72. Almost all of it is gated by `is_sm90` or an explicit opt-in. The largest are `parallel_utils/cp.py` (+183 / −4) and `v4_modules/index_attn.py` (+109 / −32).
- New files:

| New files | Lines |
| --- | --- |
| SM90 kernels in `sm90_ops/` | 3280 |
| Tests | 2134 |
| `examples/`: latency benchmark, SM90 microbenchmarks | 2365 |
| Vendor patches, including the 522-line FlashMLA CUDA patch | 656 |
| Build glue: `scripts/cuda_arch.sh`, `requirements-sm90.txt` | 24 |
| `doc/sm90.md` | 113 |

- One new submodule, `vendor/FlashMLA-SM90`, pinned at `ba89a34`.

The full write-up, including build prerequisites, layouts and settings, is in [`doc/sm90.md`](doc/sm90.md).

## Commits

1. `777aec0` platform: detect Hopper (SM90) GPUs
1. `16f7e44` build: build the SM90 (Hopper) dependencies from build.sh
1. `b1f3b7d` attention: run V4.1 sparse attention on SM90
1. `12da8e7` sm90_ops: add a block-[32, 32] FP8 GEMM for Hopper
1. `23a1290` model: route FP8 linears and wo_a to the SM90 GEMM
1. `e7024f5` sm90_ops: add the sparse-indexer MQA logits for Hopper
1. `3f9631b` model: score the sparse indexer with sm90_ops on SM90
1. `c32bf07` moe: run MXFP4 routed experts on SM90
1. `f68df48` cp: fall back to NCCL all-gather without NVLS multicast
1. `d9a9bae` examples: add an offline latency benchmark
1. `b4a8287` doc: add SM90 (Hopper) setup and results

Each commit is one reviewable step and passes ruff on its own. If smaller PRs would be easier to review, I can split the series.

## Verification

**Unit tests.** On an H20-3e host, with 4 GPUs visible for the CP tests:

```bash
pytest tests/sm90 tests/models/test_sm90_moe.py tests/distributed/test_cp_manager.py
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The command above | 162 passed, 1 skipped |
| `pytest -m ci tests/sm90 tests/models/test_sm90_moe.py tests/benchmarks` | 20 passed |
| CPU-only collection of the same paths plus `test_cp_manager.py` | 179 tests, no errors |

The skipped test is the `BucketBuffer` half of `test_cp_manager.py`, which needs NVLink multicast that this host does not have.

The tests compare each kernel with an independent fp32 reference, or with the official reference kernels in the checkpoint's `inference/` directory:

| Component | Criterion |
| --- | --- |
| Attention | cos > 0.99999, LSE error < 1e-3 |
| FP8 GEMM | cos > 0.99999 on every V4.1 shape (bf16 outputs); cos > 0.999 for the FP8-output `wo_a` einsum |
| Indexer | matches a torch restatement of the reference math within the tests' per-logit tolerances. The FP4 → FP8 re-encoding is exact when a row's block exponents span at most 14 binades, with a documented bound beyond that |
| Routed experts | cos > 0.9999 and relative error < 2% |
| CP NCCL path | bitwise equal to a reference gather. Equal to `BucketBuffer` on a host with NVLink multicast; that comparison is skipped on hosts without it |

**Layer-level numerics.** I fed each sub-module of `inference/model.py` the same inputs DeepInfer saw at that layer, for layers 20–39 with 4K and 8K prompts:

| Sub-module | Agreement with the reference |
| --- | --- |
| Attention output | cos ≥ 0.9993 |
| MoE output | cos ≥ 0.9999 |
| Gate expert ids | 100% |
| Indexer top-k recall | 0.992–0.997 |

**End to end.**

- Greedy generation (DP8 x EP8, CUDA graphs, DSpark) answers the sample prompts correctly: Beijing, Rayleigh scattering, 72, and all 25 primes below 100. The first answer matches the reference implementation token for token.
- GSM8K: 0.943 on 8 GPUs (0.941 with DSpark off), 0.941 on 4 GPUs.

**Build from scratch.** On an 8x H20-3e host, I ran `DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia ./build.sh` unmodified in a clean Python 3.12 environment (`env -i`, no `CUDA_HOME`):

- It built everything in 6 min 52 s: DeepSelect, FlashMLA-SM90, DeepEP, DeepGEMM, `deepinfer._C` and `humming-kernels` 0.1.12.
- NCCL 2.32.3 is the only NCCL in the environment.
- After the build, the vendor submodules are back at their pinned commits with no local changes.
- With an R570 driver, the CUDA 13 forward-compatibility `libcuda` must be on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- In that fresh environment, with a new `HOME` and cold JIT caches, the unit tests above give 162 passed, 1 skipped. The only `libnccl` loaded is the venv's 2.32.3; no `LD_PRELOAD` or path changes are needed.

**Lint.** `ruff check --no-cache && ruff format --check --no-cache` (ruff 0.15.0) and `bash scripts/format_csrc.sh --check` pass.

**Not tested on SM100 or Ascend.** I have no such hardware. Outside the `is_sm90` branches, the diff is limited to the following. Each item keeps the existing behaviour off SM90 by construction.

- `build.sh` and `scripts/cuda_arch.sh`: every NVIDIA build now detects the GPU architecture, defaulting to sm100 when no GPU is visible. Only the sm90 result changes what is built.
- `platform.py` and `deep_cluster/hardware/{device,nvidia}.py`: a cached `is_sm90()` NVML check runs on NVIDIA GPUs. `nvidia.py` binds one more NVML symbol (`nvmlDeviceGetName`).
- `.gitmodules`: the new `vendor/FlashMLA-SM90` submodule, built only for sm90.
- `input_metadata/{dflash,input_metadata}.py`: import `FlashMLASchedMeta` through `attention_backend`, which re-exports the same class off SM90.
- `deepinfer/environ.py`: new variables only. The defaults preserve existing behaviour.
- `parallel_utils/cp.py`: off SM90, `auto` builds `BucketBuffer` exactly as before. `DEEPINFER_CP_COMM_BACKEND=nccl` is an explicit opt-in.
- `parallel_utils/userbuffer.py`: log text only.
- `examples/offline_inference.py`: on SM90 it no longer defaults `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. The offline decode-PPL tests skip SM90, because their goldens are SM100 batch-invariant runs.
- `scripts/build_vendor.sh`: applies `scripts/vendor_patches/` during the build and reverts the patches it applied afterwards. All current patches (DeepSelect, DeepEP, FlashMLA-SM90) apply to SM90 builds only, so SM100 and Ascend build the same sources as before.

## Performance on H20-3e

All numbers come from `examples/latency_benchmark.py`, added in this PR, with these settings:

- DSpark on: `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE=5`, `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`
- `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact`, `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140`
- CUDA graphs on

The TTFT prompts were code text from an earlier version of the prompt builder. The committed builder uses Python standard-library source instead, so it produces different token inputs.

**TTFT**, in seconds. One cold request at a time, median of 3 runs after 1 warm-up, prefill intervals set to 1.

The CP all-gathers use NCCL, the SM90 default. They were measured with `DEEPINFER_CP_NCCL_OVERLAP=1`, which overlaps them with compute. The default now waits for each all-gather at launch instead. With that default, a from-scratch build of this series on another 8x H20-3e host measured 0.188 s at 1K and 2.107 s at 128K.

| Input | 1K | 4K | 16K | 64K | 128K | 256K | 512K | ~1M |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 GPUs, CP8 | 0.189 | 0.188 | 0.308 | 1.068 | 2.146 | 4.458 | 9.662 | 22.19 |
| 4 GPUs, CP4 | 0.184 | 0.190 | 0.492 | 1.791 | 3.636 | 7.641 | 16.72 | 38.48 |
| 8 GPUs, DP8 (no CP, one GPU per request) | 0.176 | 0.364 | 1.182 | 4.568 | 9.461 | 20.22 | 46.05 | 113.1 |

**Decode**, 8 GPUs, DP8 x EP8, random token ids, 1024 in / 512 out, seed 20261018. Output tok/s, with median TPOT in parentheses. For one request the rate excludes TTFT; for 32 and 64 requests it is total throughput.

| Concurrency | Default prefill intervals (70 / 100) | Prefill intervals 1 / 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 158 (6.34 ms) | 163 (6.13 ms) |
| 32 | 2618 (6.30 ms) | 2167 (9.63 ms) |
| 64 | 3793 (7.43 ms) | 2930 (14.13 ms) |

Why the two columns differ:

- With intervals 1 / 1, every new request starts its prefill at once. DP ranks advance in lockstep, so the other ranks run slower decode steps meanwhile.
- The default intervals batch those prefills. Under load, this cuts the median TPOT by 35–47%.
- Profiling with 4K-in / 1K-out coding prompts puts the steady-state decode step at about 33–34 ms. The gap between the columns is prefill interference, not kernel time.

**4 GPUs**, DP4 x EP4, random token ids (seed 0), 1024 in / 512 out, prefill intervals 1 / 1:

| Concurrency | Total output tok/s |
| --- | --- |
| 32 | 1981 |
| 64 | 2463 |

## Environment

| Item | Version |
| --- | --- |
| GPUs | 8x / 4x NVIDIA H20-3e (141 GB, NVLink), SM90 |
| Driver | R570 with CUDA 13 forward compatibility, and R590 |
| CUDA / PyTorch | CUDA 13.0–13.2, torch 2.13.0 |
| Vendored | DeepGEMM 1fc9c66, DeepEP 93eb6eb, DeepSelect bfa4507 (+ `scripts/vendor_patches/`), FlashMLA ba89a34 (+ V4.1 patch) |
| SM90 extras | `humming-kernels==0.1.12` (default MoE backend when installed) |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, unmodified |
| Code | Performance and accuracy numbers come from integration builds of this series, before the history was squashed into these commits; the kernels and model wiring are the same, and the CP rows used the overlapped NCCL mode (see TTFT). The unit tests and the from-scratch build ran on a release candidate. It differs from these commits only in comments, docs, test file names, the benchmark prompt builder, the SM90 default of `examples/offline_inference.py`, and patch bookkeeping in `build_vendor.sh`. |

## Reproduce

```bash
export DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia
./build.sh                       # detects SM90; or set DEEPINFER_CUDA_ARCH=sm90
pytest tests/sm90 tests/models/test_sm90_moe.py tests/distributed/test_cp_manager.py
python examples/offline_inference.py

export DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE=5 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1
export DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140

# TTFT, CP8, prefill intervals 1 for single-request latency.
# DEEPINFER_CP_NCCL_OVERLAP=1 matches the measured setting; omit it for the default.
DEEPINFER_CP_NCCL_OVERLAP=1 DEEPINFER_PREFILL_ATTEMPT_INTERVAL=1 DEEPINFER_PREFILL_ANY_ATTEMPT_INTERVAL=1 \
  python examples/latency_benchmark.py --ep 8 --cp 8 --suites ttft --out_dir runs/ttft-cp8

# Decode, DP8 x EP8, random ids 1024 in / 512 out, default prefill intervals
python examples/latency_benchmark.py --ep 8 --suites single,concurrency --prompt random --seed 20261018 \
  --decode_input_len 1024 --decode_output_len 512 --concurrency 32 64 --out_dir runs/decode-dp8

# GSM8K, SGLang's shot layout: the first 8 test questions are shots, and all 1319 are scored
python examples/latency_benchmark.py --ep 8 --suites gsm8k --gsm8k_data test.jsonl --gsm8k_overlap_shots \
  --out_dir runs/gsm8k
```

## Notes for reviewers

- **Dependencies.**
  - `humming-kernels` (PyPI, Apache-2.0) is imported lazily, only on SM90 and only by the humming / hybrid MoE backends. Without it, `auto` uses the pure-Triton `triton_fp8` backend. That backend needs about twice the expert memory, so it fits at EP8 but not at EP4.
  - `flash_mla_sm90` is built from a patch on FlashMLA `ba89a34`. I am happy to send the patch to FlashMLA instead.
  - The DeepSelect and DeepEP patches (SM90 builds only) are candidates for those projects.
- **Indexer numerics.** The SM90 indexer follows the reference implementation's arithmetic, including an fp32 head sum. Its top-k picks can therefore differ from SM100 on near-ties.
- **Not ported.** The SM100-only fused kernels (Mega MoE, `mega_gate`, `mega_mhc`, candidate-sparse MQA) are not ported; SM90 uses the existing non-mega paths.
- **Known gaps.**
  - Single-request TTFT has a floor of about 0.19 s for prompts up to 8K tokens, because short prefills run eagerly and are bound by launch overhead.
  - On hosts where NVLink multicast works, setting `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1` lets CP use DeepEP's `BucketBuffer`. That was 3–5% faster than the default NCCL path at long context.
- **Open PRs touching the same code.**
  - #60 (vendor registry) and #88 change `get_bf16_tflops_limit`, as this PR does. If either lands first, I will rebase.
  - `PLATFORM.is_sm90` is a capability flag on the existing GPU platform, not a new `PlatformEnum` member, in line with the direction in #63.
- **Not verified.**
  - SM100 and Ascend were not run; I have no such hardware. Those paths are unchanged by construction, apart from the items listed above.
  - Hopper parts other than H20-3e, and multi-node runs, were not tested.
- **Follow-ups.**
  - A DeepEP change that lets `BucketBuffer` all-gather without multicast. It is prototyped and bitwise-checked, but not included here.
  - A faster candidate-row indexer kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.15.0) and `scripts/format_csrc.sh --check` pass
- [x] New tests under `tests/`; SM90-only tests skip elsewhere
- [x] Unit, numerics and end-to-end results on SM90 hardware
- [x] SM100 / Ascend code paths unchanged (gated by `PLATFORM.is_sm90`); not run on SM100 hardware
- [x] Documentation: `doc/sm90.md`
